To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the regional topography can control the location of the hydrothermal zone and the associated heat transfer, and that this effect depends on the average permeability.

(i) topography plays an important role in the emplacement of a hydrothermal system, even if the permeability is homogeneous, (ii) the location of hot springs is controlled by the topographic gradient and the permeability of the volcanic edifice and (iii) the average permeability can be constrained from the position of hot springs.
The remote emplacement of the hot springs at the Ticsani and the Ubinas volcanos can be explained by the influence of the topographic gradient.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the influence of the edifice topography on the emplacement of a hydrothermal system, and the possibility to constrain the permeability of a volcano from geothermal data.
the understanding of hydrothermal systems in the framework of a complex geothermal environment.
the understanding of the emplacement of hydrothermally active areas at volcanoes and their relation to the regional topography.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the regional topography is a key factor influencing fluid flow in volcanic areas.

the hydrothermal systems can be emplaced far away from the top of the volcano, even for a low permeability of the volcanic edifice, and that the regional topography is the key controlling factor of this phenomenon.
the topography is an important factor in determining the location of the hydrothermal activity in a volcano.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hydrothermal system emplacement is not only a function of the permeability structure of the volcanic edifice, but it is also influenced by the regional topographic gradients.
the regional topography can significantly influence the fluid flow pattern, even in the presence of a strong heat source.
the hydrothermal systems can be located at the foot of an edifice even if they are not centered on the volcano top.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hydrothermal systems can be emplaced at large distance from the heat sources in case of high permeability of the subsurface.
the regional topography is a major factor controlling the emplacement of a hydrothermal system and the associated heat transfer in the subsurface.
regional topographic gradients have to be considered as important controls of fluid flow in the subsurface.
